title: Tell the story from the pictures
description: Pick a picture book and cover the words. Now tell the story using only the pictures. What do you think happens on each page?

body.heading: Look before you tell
paragraphs: Choose a book you know, or a new one. Cover the words with your hand, or just don't read them. Look at the first picture for a long time. Who is in it? Where are they? How do they feel?
Now tell that part of the story out loud, in your own words. Turn the page and do it again. The pictures will give you clues — faces, colours, and little details hiding in the corners.

body.heading: Check the real story
paragraphs: When you finish, read the book again with the words. Did the pictures tell you the same story? Which parts did you guess right, and which parts surprised you?
Making up the story first is not getting it wrong. It is reading with your eyes before you read with words — and it makes the real story feel like a prize.

takeaway: Cover the words, tell the story from the pictures alone, then read the real words and see what you guessed.
materials: A picture book with clear, detailed pictures
Your hand, to cover the words (optional)
supervision: A grown-up listens to the child's story, asks gentle questions about the pictures, and reads the real words afterwards.
safetyNotes: This is a calm indoor reading activity — choose a comfy spot with good light so eyes do not strain.
screenFreeExtension: Draw three pictures of something that happened today, in order, and tell your day as a story from your own pictures.
